I am 63 years old and I have farmed these 10.1 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years, ever since I finished middle school. My household is just me and my wife now — our children work in factories in the city. I have 7 mu that I rotate wheat and maize on, and 3.1 mu that I plant cotton.

My wheat went into the ground last October. I did rotary tillage first, then sowed improved wheat seed. For the base fertilizer I spread 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu — that is one bag for every two mu, roughly. Now it is April and the wheat is at jointing. I will topdress with 40 jin of urea per mu, exactly what I did last year when I got 450 kg per mu. My neighbor across the road only used 25 jin of urea and his wheat turned yellow and thin. I will not take that risk. Fertilizer costs money, yes — a bag of urea is over 100 yuan now — but losing a whole crop is a disaster. For the year I will irrigate three times: the winter irrigation is already done, then one now at jointing, one at heading, and one at grain filling if May is dry. Two pesticide sprays is what I always do. I expect about 450 kg per mu again.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize on those same 7 mu. Everyone here uses hybrid seed — I switched years ago after I saw my neighbor's hybrid maize outyield my old seed by a wide margin. There is no time to plow; we direct-seed with no-tillage right after the wheat comes out because the season is short. I will put down 80 jin per mu of compound fertilizer at sowing, then topdress with 50 jin per mu of urea at the jointing stage. Two irrigations in summer should be enough, and two pesticide sprays. Last year I got 520 kg per mu. If I match that I will be satisfied.

For cotton, I have 3.1 mu. I will rotary till in late April and plant hybrid Bt cotton seed. Cotton is more work but the price is usually decent. I will apply 60 jin per mu of compound fertilizer at planting and topdress twice with urea. Cotton needs more potassium, so I make sure to get compound fertilizer with higher potassium content — the dealer told me that years ago and it worked. Three irrigations and three pesticide sprays; cotton always needs more care than grain. Last year I harvested 260 kg per mu of seed cotton. That is good money for the effort.

I watch every yuan. With only two of us and fertilizer prices high, I think hard about each purchase. But I learned this lesson long ago: skimping on inputs is false economy. Better to put down a bit too much fertilizer than to watch your crop fail. My neighbor Wang applies about the same amounts as me, and his yields are steady, so I know I am in the right range. Change is risky; what worked before will work again.
